why: Pages are nodes and links are directed edges, each click costing 1, so the minimum clicks from start to target is a BFS over get_links(page) on the directed graph.
hints: Each click has the same cost. Which traversal gives the fewest clicks?
Build get_links as a dict page -> list of linked pages, then BFS from start until you pop target.
Parse m, the m edges and the final 'start target' line; BFS with a visited set; output [str(distance)] or ["-1"]. O(m).
pitfalls: Links are directed: A -> B does not let you go from B to A.
start == target answers 0 even if the page has no links.
Return a list of output lines of strings, e.g. ["2"], not an int.
statement:
The function receives the whole standard input as one string and returns the output lines as a list of strings.

Input format:

  • Line 1: integer m, the number of directed links.
  • Next m lines: u v, a link from page u to page v.
  • Last line: start target.

Implement get_links(page) returning every x with a link page -> x, and use it to find the minimum number of clicks (one click follows one outgoing link) from start to target. Output one line: that number, 0 if start == target, or -1 if target cannot be reached.

Example: links A->B, B->C, A->D, D->C, C->E, query A C.

  • 0 clicks: {A}.
  • 1 click: get_links(A) = {B, D}.
  • 2 clicks: get_links(B) and get_links(D) both contain C, so C is reached.

Output: ["2"].
